recall_prompt: Say how you would find (fofof)(x) — what happens when f is applied twice, and what the third application gives.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply f twice
steps.margin_note: First mark. Everything in this question follows from (fof)(x) = x, so write the numerator and the denominator as single fractions before cancelling.
steps.memory_tip: Applying f twice gives x back. A function like this is its own inverse.

recall.must_convey: That f applied to f(x) simplifies to x, because the numerator becomes 2x/(x − 1) and the denominator becomes 2/(x − 1).
accept: f of f of x is f of x plus one over f of x minus one which simplifies to x
the top becomes two x over x minus one and the bottom two over x minus one so you get x
applying f twice gives back x
f rendu sarlu apply chesthe x ye vastundi
f o f of x equals x because the x minus one cancels
reject: the third one gives f of x
heard_as: two x over x minus one

steps.why: Both the numerator and the denominator carry the factor 1/(x − 1), so that factor cancels and only 2x over 2 is left. f itself needs x ≠ 1, and the question also rules out x = −1, so every line here is written for x ≠ ±1.
common_mistakes: Adding 1 to only the numerator of f(x) instead of to the whole fraction.
Cancelling x − 1 before the top and the bottom are written as single fractions.

steps.label: Apply f once more
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three copies of f are one (fof) followed by one f. Since (fof)(x) = x, the last f acts on x itself.
steps.memory_tip: Count the f's: an even number gives x, an odd number gives f(x).

recall.must_convey: That the third f acts on x, so (fofof)(x) is f(x) itself, which is (x + 1)/(x − 1).
accept: since f o f gives x the third f acts on x so the answer is f of x
f o f o f of x is f of x which is x plus one over x minus one
three applications leave one f so the answer is the original function
rendu sarlu x vastundi so moodava sari f of x vastundi
the answer is x plus one by x minus one
heard_as: x plus one over x minus one

steps.why: Three copies of f split as one pair plus one single. The pair returns its input unchanged, so only the single f is left to act. Checking at x = 2 gives 3, and (2 + 1)/(2 − 1) = 3, which agrees.
common_mistakes: Answering x, which is what an even number of applications gives, not three.
Leaving the condition x ≠ ±1 off the final line.
